text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand. When developers refactor, they clean up messy sections, remove repeated parts, and give variables clearer names. This makes the code simpler for everyone on the team. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which is the extra work that builds up when code is written quickly without care. By refactoring regularly, teams can fix small problems before they become big ones. Remember, refactoring should never change how the program behaves—only how it looks inside.
